3.2 Quantized State Storage We compute each recurrent update in the model’s default compute precision and quantize the resulting state before writing it to persistent GPU memory.
For integer storage, we use per-block asymmetric affine quantization.
For a block 𝒙 {\bm{x}} with extrema x min x_{\min} and x max x_{\max} , define s = ( x max − x min ) / ( 2 b − 1 ) s=(x_{\max}-x_{\min})/(2^{b}-1) and z = round ( − x min / s ) z=\operatorname{round}(-x_{\min}/s) . The stored code and its reconstruction are: q i = round ⁡ ( x i / s ) + z , Q b ​ ( x i ) = s ⋅ ( q i − z ) . q_{i}=\operatorname{round}(x_{i}/s)+z,\qquad Q_{b}(x_{i})=s\cdot(q_{i}-z). (3) We use b = 8 b=8 for INT8 and b = 4 b=4 for INT4.
Specifications for all evaluated formats are provided in Appendix A.1 .

into contiguous blocks. Quantization parameters are recomputed whenever the
state is written. Integer formats. INT8 and INT4 use the asymmetric affine mapping in
Equation 3 with groups of 32 values. The scale and
zero point are stored in FP16, and integer codes saturate to the available
unsigned range. The Hadamard variants apply a normalized block- 32 32 transform
before quantization and its inverse after reconstruction. Floating-point formats. FP8 uses E4M3 ( Micikevicius et al., 2022 ) in the natural domain, with one FP32

A.2 Calibration Protocol Calibration uses 32 documents from the validation split of the
Pile ( Gao et al., 2020 ) . We sample eight documents from each of four domains:
DM Mathematics, PubMed Abstracts, GitHub, and StackExchange. Each document is
truncated to 256 tokens and evaluated once with teacher forcing. Recurrent
states are sampled every eight tokens, giving 256 samples per domain and 1,024
samples per recurrent layer. Let 𝒟 \mathcal{D} denote the four calibration domains and let Ω d \Omega_{d} contain
the sampled state writes from domain d d . We use the domain-balanced empirical
expectation 𝔼 cal ​ [ f ] = 1 | 𝒟 | ​ ∑ d ∈ 𝒟 1 | Ω d | ​ ∑ ( x , t ) ∈ Ω d f ⁡ ( x , t ) . \mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{cal}}[f]=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}|}\sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}}\frac{1}{|\Omega_{d}|}\sum_{(x,t)\in\Omega_{d}}f(x,t). (13) For one recurrent layer and head, let a x , t , u = [ 𝚲 x , t ] u ​ u a_{x,t,u}=[{\bm{\Lambda}}_{x,t}]_{uu} . We estimate the two score components as ℰ u \displaystyle\mathcal{E}_{u} = 𝔼 cal [ ‖ [ Q lo ( 𝑺 x , t ) ] u : − 𝑺 x , t , u : ‖ 2 2 ] , \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{cal}}\!\left[\left\|[Q_{\mathrm{lo}}({\bm{S}}_{x,t})]_{u:}-{\bm{S}}_{x,t,u:}\right\|_{2}^{2}\right], (14) a eff , u \displaystyle a_{\mathrm{eff},u} = exp ⁡ ( 𝔼 cal ​ [ log ⁡ a x , t , u ] ) , 𝒫 u = 1 max ⁡ { 1 − a eff , u 2 , τ } , \displaystyle=\exp\!\left(\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{cal}}[\log a_{x,t,u}]\right),\qquad\mathcal{P}_{u}=\frac{1}{\max\!\left\{1-a_{\mathrm{eff},u}^{2},\tau\right\}}, (15) with τ = 10 − 4 \tau=10^{-4} . Here Q lo Q_{\mathrm{lo}} is the deployed storage mapping
specified in Appendix A.1 . Algorithm 1 applies
these estimates independently to every layer and head. Calibration uses only
state and decay statistics from this corpus; no downstream evaluation data are
used. The resulting key-channel indices are fixed after calibration. Calibration cost. Calibration is performed on a dual-socket Intel Xeon 6767P server using 64 CPU
threads. Excluding model-loading time, processing all 32 documents takes
approximately 7 minutes for Qwen3.6-35B (GDN) and 9 minutes for
Kimi-Linear-48B (KDA). Calibration is run once per checkpoint, and the
resulting layout is reused for all inference requests.

A.5 Packed Layout and Fused Update Persistent representation. Let π ℓ , h \pi_{\ell,h} be the key-channel permutation obtained during calibration. We
apply this permutation consistently to the state and all key-channel-indexed operands,
placing the K hi = 16 K_{\mathrm{hi}}=16 protected key channels before the low-precision key channels. For one
layer, head, and request slot, the persistent cache is represented as ℬ ℓ , h \displaystyle\mathcal{B}_{\ell,h} = ( 𝑺 hi , 𝑸 lo , 𝑴 lo ) , \displaystyle=({\bm{S}}^{\mathrm{hi}},{\bm{Q}}^{\mathrm{lo}},{\bm{M}}^{\mathrm{lo}}), (17) 𝑺 hi \displaystyle{\bm{S}}^{\mathrm{hi}} ∈ FP16 K hi × d v , 𝑸 lo ∈ UINT8 ( d k − K hi ) × d v , \displaystyle\in\mathrm{FP16}^{K_{\mathrm{hi}}\times d_{v}},\qquad{\bm{Q}}^{\mathrm{lo}}\in\mathrm{UINT8}^{(d_{k}-K_{\mathrm{hi}})\times d_{v}}, 𝑴 lo \displaystyle{\bm{M}}^{\mathrm{lo}} ∈ FP16 ( d k − K hi ) × ( d v / G ) × 2 . \displaystyle\in\mathrm{FP16}^{(d_{k}-K_{\mathrm{hi}})\times(d_{v}/G)\times 2}. where G = 32 G=32 and the final metadata dimension stores the affine scale and zero
point. 𝑸 lo {\bm{Q}}^{\mathrm{lo}} contains the codes produced after the block-Hadamard
transform. A checkpoint stores one copy of π ℓ , h \pi_{\ell,h} as model
metadata. This produces dense, contiguous precision regions accessed with
regular vector loads and stores. The KDA executor further uses a
value-block-major organization that co-locates each 32-value code tile with its
scale and zero point. Fused decode executor. The fused CUDA executor performs the complete state transition in one kernel.
It consumes recurrent inputs in the calibrated key-channel order, loads the
FP16 and UINT8 state regions, reconstructs low-precision tiles, and evaluates
the recurrence in FP32. Before writeback, the kernel computes blockwise
minima and maxima, derives new affine parameters, requantizes the low-precision
tier, and writes both regions directly to ℬ ℓ , h \mathcal{B}_{\ell,h} . The layout maps the mixed-precision update to coalesced memory transactions.
The executor vectorizes over pairs of value lanes,
uses instruction-level UINT8 unpacking and saturating packing, and retains
recently consumed state tiles in registers across recurrence phases. Shared
memory stages the compressed codes and their metadata. Prefill path. Prefill evaluates the recurrence in FP32 within each chunk, then writes the
chunk-final state directly into the same packed cache defined in
Equation 17 . Subsequent prefill chunks and decoding
steps read that compressed representation.
